facts.detail: Customers should receive estimated speeds for busy periods: 8–10pm for residential services and 12–2pm for business services.
A provider signed to the code should give a personalised minimum guaranteed broadband speed before purchase.
If a network speed problem remains below the guaranteed level, the provider has 30 days to fix it before the code's exit protection applies.
Where the provider cannot resolve the qualifying network-speed problem within 30 days, the customer can leave without an early-exit fee.

guard_streams.write_limit: A sales estimate or contractual guarantee is not a measured parcel speed and cannot populate current coverage.

facts.detail: The updated broadband speeds codes apply to broadband purchases from 21 December 2022.
The current residential list includes BT, EE, NOW Broadband, PlusNet, Sky, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Zen Internet.
The current business-code list on the overview names BT, TalkTalk and Virgin Media.
The 2022 update aligns the right to exit for broadband and bundled services with revised General Conditions implemented from 17 June 2022.

guard_streams.write_limit: Voluntary-code membership and contract remedies do not prove address serviceability or observed performance.

facts.detail: Phone, broadband and pay-TV minimum contract periods are commonly 12, 18 or 24 months.
Providers must send end-of-contract information between 10 and 40 days before the minimum term ends.
The notification includes the end date, leaving notice period, current price and post-contract price.
The notification includes the provider's best deals, including new-customer prices, and end dates for other bundled contracts.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract status and tariff notifications are customer-account evidence, not network coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Customers who remain out of contract must receive an annual reminder and updated best-deal information.
Ofcom's end-of-contract notification rules took effect in February 2020.
Ofcom's analysis reported a 13-percentage-point renewal increase for Plusnet and roughly 10 points for BT, EE and Virgin Media after alerts.
The research found that some customers saved more than £110 a year after taking a new deal in response to an alert.

guard_streams.write_limit: Historical renewal effects and savings cannot be converted into parcel-level price, speed or coverage.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Network and Service Resilience Guidance statement

facts.detail: The Network and Service Resilience Guidance page was last updated on 16 June 2026.
The guidance uses a principles-based approach intended to apply broadly across public electronic communications networks and services.
It covers architecture, design and operational practices that underpin robust networks and services.
Ofcom clarified expectations for mobile-network backup-power arrangements in radio access networks.

guard_streams.write_limit: Resilience expectations and provider architecture controls do not establish uninterrupted service at any parcel.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Network and Service Resilience Guidance statement

facts.detail: Ofcom identifies telecoms–energy interdependency as a major resilience focus.
Ofcom worked with industry, government and Ofgem to improve coordination during major incidents.
The telecoms Electronic Communication Resilience and Response Group and the Energy Networks Association improved planning, communication and coordination.
The guidance notes future resilience improvements may include satellite capabilities and devices connecting across multiple networks.

guard_streams.write_limit: Sector-level resilience initiatives are not live outage telemetry or parcel uptime guarantees.

facts.detail: The monitoring programme opened on 11 July 2022 and closed on 20 July 2023.
The relevant rule is General Condition A3.2(b), requiring necessary measures for uninterrupted access to emergency organisations.
Ofcom gathered information from more than 30 communications providers, including network, broadband and VoIP providers.
The programme found no significant compliance concern requiring formal investigation and reported provider improvements.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compliance-programme outcomes cannot be used as proof of power resilience or availability at a specific parcel.

facts.detail: The May 2026 Suffolk redesign revised the contract to around 60,000 premises.
The redesigned Suffolk contract is backed by up to £118.2 million.
The original award described around 79,500 premises.
The redesign followed expanded commercial rollout and changed market conditions to minimise overlap.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional contract scope and investment are planned programme evidence, not current parcel orderability.

facts.detail: The May 2026 Norfolk redesign revised the contract to around 33,000 premises.
The redesigned Norfolk contract is backed by £61.9 million.
The original award covered around 62,200 premises with a £114.2 million contract.
Preparatory trenching, duct and fibre work must occur before residents or businesses can request service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract inclusion or preparatory construction does not prove completed service at an individual address.

facts.detail: The May 2026 Hampshire redesign revised the contract to around 29,000 premises.
The redesigned Hampshire contract is backed by £71.7 million.
The original contract described around 75,500 premises.
Detailed planning and technical constraints can change scope, and connection requests follow network construction.

guard_streams.write_limit: A redesigned target count cannot be promoted to exact current parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The May 2026 redesign revised the Leicestershire and Warwickshire contract to around 36,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by up to £76.4 million.
The original award described around 38,000 premises.
The redesign focuses subsidy on premises otherwise likely to miss out and reduces overlap with commercial rollout.

guard_streams.write_limit: Programme targeting and subsidy rationale do not establish live parcel service.

facts.detail: The May 2026 redesign revised the contract to around 6,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £19.8 million.
The original award described around 25,000 premises.
Premises may be outside scope because service exists, commercial or voucher plans apply, or cost and engineering difficulty are too high.

guard_streams.write_limit: Exclusion reasons and redesigned scope cannot determine current availability for a parcel without accepted evidence.

facts.detail: BDUK awarded Gigaclear two Project Gigabit contracts for North and South Oxfordshire.
The combined Oxfordshire contracts target around 10,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The combined contract value is £26.5 million.
The contracts were signed in November 2023.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award and signature records are not evidence that construction is complete or service is orderable.

facts.detail: The Derbyshire Project Gigabit contract was awarded to Connect Fibre.
The award targets more than 17,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract value is £33 million.
The page states construction precedes connection requests and contract premises can change after detailed planning or for technical reasons.

guard_streams.write_limit: A procurement award and anticipated build sequence do not prove current parcel availability.
